name: Sable Noir Mango-Habanero Tablets
manufacturer: Sable Noir Artisan Confections (Tier 3-4 boutique brand)
description: Dark synth-cocoa tablets with embedded mango-habanero flavor pockets — thin squares scored for breaking, packaged in matte black paper with a single-color foil fruit emboss. Sable Noir's deliberately restrained packaging is part of the brand's premium positioning.
flavor_profile: Deep bitter synth-cocoa with bright mango sweetness that erupts from flavor pockets mid-chew, followed by a slow habanero heat bloom that builds for thirty seconds after swallowing
cultural_context: Sable Noir occupies the sweet spot between accessible luxury and genuine craft. Tier 3 consumers buy it for special occasions; Tier 4 consumers keep it on the desk as a signal of taste. The delayed habanero heat is a conversation piece — first-time eaters often don't react immediately, then visibly register the warmth, which experienced eaters watch for with quiet satisfaction.
story_hooks: A Sable Noir tablet given as a gift contained something embedded in the foil wrapping — not the candy itself, but the packaging — visible only under specific spectrum light.
Sable Noir's boutique production facility sits in a Tier 3 building with an unusual sub-basement; the confectioners above have no idea what's below them.
A food critic's scathing review of a Sable Noir competitor has been traced to a sponsored placement, and the Sable Noir brand manager is the connection — but the critic doesn't know they were used.
